finding.claim: Missing authorization enforcement: update_doc calls can_edit() but discards the boolean result, so any user can overwrite any document body. The sibling update_title correctly uses require_edit().
finding.source: Any request to PUT /doc/<doc_id> with JSON body {"body": ...} and any doc_id that exists, from a user who is neither owner nor editor
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20 (write to the document)

trace.note: Route PUT /doc/<doc_id> registered, no auth decorator
doc fetched from DOCS by attacker-supplied id
can_edit(g.user, doc) returns False for non-editors but the return value is ignored; no abort(403)

finding.guards_checked: can_edit is called but its result unused; require_edit (which aborts 403) is not used here; no before_request hook or decorator in the file enforces access; compare update_title at line 27 which is guarded correctly.

verdict.guard_found: none effective: can_edit() at docs.py:19 returns a bool that is discarded; require_edit (docs.py:11-13) aborts 403 but is only used in update_title at line 27; no before_request hook or decorator exists in the directory.
verdict.reason: docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement with the result discarded, so docs.py:20 overwrites doc["body"] for any caller, unlike update_title which calls require_edit at docs.py:27.
